pageTitle: Tube Amplifiers: The Heart of Rock & Roll
subtitle: The gold standard of guitar amplification - warmth, dynamics, and vintage tone

introduction.title: Tube Amplifiers: The Heart of Rock & Roll
introduction.text: Discover why vacuum tube amplifiers remain the preferred choice of professional musicians worldwide.

columns.title: What You'll Learn
columns.text: How vacuum tubes create their legendary warm tone. Different tube types and their sonic characteristics. Famous tube amplifiers and their signature sounds. Maintenance, care, and tube replacement. Why tubes still matter in the digital age.

cards.title: Vacuum Tube Technology
cards.description: Vacuum tubes, invented in the early 1900s, amplify electrical signals by controlling the flow of electrons through a vacuum. This process creates the warm, musical distortion that guitarists love.
items: Cathode: Heated element that emits electrons
Anode: Attracts electrons, completing the circuit
Grid: Controls electron flow, creating amplification

cards.title: The Tube Amp Signal Chain
cards.description: Understanding the signal path helps you appreciate how each stage contributes to the final tone.
items: Input: Guitar signal enters the first preamp tube
Preamp: Multiple tube stages shape and color the tone
Power tubes: Amplify the signal to drive speakers
Output transformer: Matches impedance to speakers

cards.title: Preamp Tubes
items: 12AX7 (ECC83): High gain, bright tone. Most common preamp tube.
12AU7 (ECC82): Lower gain, warmer tone. Often used in reverb circuits.
12AT7 (ECC81): Medium gain, balanced tone. Good for phase inverters.

cards.title: Power Tubes
items: EL34: British sound, compressed midrange. Used in Marshall amps.
6L6: American tone, tight bass, clear highs. Fender's choice.
KT88: High power, excellent headroom. Used in high-end amps.

cards.title: Tonal Warmth
cards.description: Tubes produce even-order harmonics that sound musical and pleasing to the ear, creating the legendary "warmth" that digital technology struggles to replicate.

cards.title: Dynamic Response
cards.description: Tube amps respond to your playing dynamics like no other amplification technology, rewarding technique and touch sensitivity.

cards.title: Natural Overdrive
cards.description: When pushed, tubes distort in a musical way that enhances rather than masks the original signal, creating the classic rock and blues tones.

cards.title: Classic American Amps
items: Fender Twin Reverb: The gold standard for clean tone. Used by countless country, jazz, and rock players. Notable users: Eric Johnson, Mark Knopfler
Fender Deluxe Reverb: Perfect balance of clean headroom and natural tube breakup. Studio favorite. Notable users: John Mayer, Keith Richards

cards.title: British Legends
items: Marshall JCM800: The sound of 80s rock and metal. Aggressive midrange and singing sustain. Notable users: Slash, Zakk Wylde
Vox AC30: Chimey, bright tone with beautiful natural compression. The Beatles' choice. Notable users: Brian May, The Edge

sections.title: Tube Amp Maintenance
sections.warningText: Tube amplifiers contain high voltages that can be lethal. Always have qualified technicians perform internal maintenance and repairs. Never remove the chassis while plugged in. Capacitors can hold charge even when unplugged. Always use proper safety procedures.

cards.title: Routine Maintenance
items: Tube replacement: Every 1-3 years depending on use
Bias adjustment: When replacing power tubes
Cleaning: Keep vents clear of dust and debris
Transport care: Remove tubes for long moves
